measurement.auditor: Olivares AI Community documentation source review

jobs.mustProve: Current session fields, conditional goal and ordered timeline; governed work-item and handoff controls; explicit limits on unqualified task-progress semantics.
Community route refusal naming Business, stored orchestration data export, deny-closed A2A delegation.
Mock runner, configured backend attestation, ordered-replay precondition.
Candidate order, fallback, deny-closed execution, exact provider/version matrix.
Local render, validate and dry-run, single-document gateway pull, Business refusal of fleet routes, and real host before/after state for any promoted delivery path.
Canonical/rendered set equality and accepted evidence for every Built alias.

evidenceFormat.note: No artifact carrying every required field at the exact refs means the claim cannot be accepted. Its absence does not block publishing the claim honestly as implemented_unaccepted.

claims.title: Live operations and sessions
claims.boundedProposition: Observe current action, model, tokens, cost and an ordered event timeline for a session. Governed work-item APIs and the handoff offer and response APIs exist and have defined component tests, which were not executed for this measurement; neither is claim-accepted. The session record keeps a goal field that no inspected writer sets, so a goal is normally absent.
conditions: The session schema records current action, model, tokens, cost and event/timeline data.
A goal is shown only when a stored record carries one; no inspected connector or module writes it.

Governed work-item routes have separate read, write and admin permissions. Work items, dependencies, acceptance criteria, events, leases, decisions and administrative event replay are separate surfaces; the work stream observes their events.

Handoff offer and response routes stay off until communication readiness holds. An offer and a response each execute in one transaction that locks the bound work item and its single work lease, refuses a work item from another workspace lineage, and is idempotent against a stored command receipt. Owner cancellation and deadline expiry exist as transaction code with component tests; no route or worker reaches them in Community.
unpromoted: An accepted task-progress journey: current live-session fields and the work-item APIs are separate source inventories; this measurement does not establish a combined task-progress invariant.
Claim-level acceptance: the work-item and handoff behavior below is source and component-test inventory, not an executed claim-acceptance run.
Workflow-driven work tasks and handoffs: orchestration is a Business capability, and Community composes no workflow caller.
gaps: The live-operation component test covers ingestion and observable state. It does not bind the published sentence to a user journey, and it was not executed for this measurement.
Owner cancellation has no route and the deadline expiry worker is not wired, so neither runs in a Community engine; their component tests call the transaction directly.

claims.title: Agent communication and orchestration
claims.boundedProposition: Orchestration and A2A delegation are Business capabilities. Community keeps the orchestration route contracts and the stored orchestration data. Every orchestration route is registered with its declared permission and answers 501 naming Business. The orchestration command answers its help and otherwise exits with the edition code. A2A delegation, inbound A2A and A2A push are refused before any request reaches a peer.
conditions: Every orchestration route answers 501 with an unavailable code and a sentence naming Business; no route handler reads or writes orchestration data.
Community runs no scheduling, cadence scan or workflow advance: those hooks do nothing and no background pump is constructed.
Stored orchestration declarations, runs and relations keep their schema, remain readable through store export and still count in account retirement; no Community route creates or edits them.
The orchestration command is hidden from Community help; asking for its help answers and exits zero, and any other argument exits with the edition code.
Community A2A send, delegation, task, inbound and push operations return a Business refusal; a configured inbound A2A server or push receiver is logged and not mounted.
The orchestration and session modules do not depend on each other.
unpromoted: Visualizing observed delegation topology and running bounded workflows are Business capabilities; their Business source is not reviewed here.
Claim-level acceptance for the public sentence at its route.
gaps: Component tests cover route refusal, stored export, command refusal and deny-closed delegation; this review did not execute them, and no test covers the gateway refusal for inbound A2A and push. None binds the public sentence to a route, conditions, exact refs, a mutant or retained evidence.
The A2A connector's package documentation still describes delegation, emission and push files that the Community source does not contain.

claims.title: Simulation sandbox
claims.boundedProposition: Run operator-authored mock scenarios and session replays in the in-process mock runner by default, or in a configured gVisor or Firecracker backend. The composition root constructs those backends only when configuration declares them; when backends are configured, runs use the first one that passes its preflight check, and every run is refused when none passes, instead of falling back to the in-process runner. Each run records the runner that executed it and the isolation that runner declares; the in-process mock runner declares isolation by construction, not operating-system isolation.
conditions: Default behavior is operator-authored mock scenario execution in the built-in in-process runner.

Operating-system isolation applies only when an isolation backend is configured and passes its preflight check. With no backend configured, scenario runs and replays use the in-process mock runner, which does not provide it.
Ordered replay depends on an ordered history source.
unpromoted: Real-agent execution: neither the mock runner nor the configured backends run an agent; both resolve scenario steps against the scenario's mocks.
Accepted journeys for local synthetic-data generation and the console scenario lifecycle. The local generator expands bounded templates; this is not model-generated synthetic data.

Attested OS isolation: this source review supplies no executed backend attestation. Backend construction and preflight code are source inventory only. Preflight checks that the backend binary runs, and for Firecracker that hardware virtualization is present; it does not exercise isolation.
gaps: This source review supplies no backend attestation artifact; configured gVisor or Firecracker construction is source inventory only.
The sandbox run record keeps the runner name, its declared isolation flag and the destroyed flag; the runtime's per-run hardening and egress attestation is not persisted with the run.

claims.title: Models, providers and routing
claims.boundedProposition: Define cost, latency, capability or pinned policies and resolve an ordered fallback chain. POST /routing-policies/{id}/execute requires the models:routing:admin permission and is deny-closed when execution is not configured. A policy without an execution profile uses the Claude Messages executor, which serves only Anthropic targets and tries the chain in order. A policy with an execution profile selects a separate Chat text port on the same route that serves only the pinned target, composed only under explicit development activation with a profile registry and readiness checks.
conditions: Policy resolution produces an ordered candidate chain.

The module always resolves a route and acts only through one of two deny-closed ports: the routing executor, composed only when an inference credential is configured, and the separate Chat port, composed only under the development activation. Until one is composed, routing resolves without any provider call.

The unprofiled executor speaks Claude Messages, directly or through a configured gateway base URL, and refuses a non-Anthropic target. The profiled Chat text port requires OLIVARES_MODEL_GATEWAY_CHAT_MODE=development_precheck and a profile registry; otherwise, or until its dependencies are bound, profiled execution returns 503, and an unknown mode value stops startup. Neither branch establishes a universal provider or model matrix.

The operation applies its admission, stop, model-governance, scope and model-access checks before execution. The unprofiled branch then consults the composed FinOps admission gate; in Community it enforces only budgets already stored, while the FinOps module is on, because Community cannot create or change a budget. The development Chat branch runs its separate ordered content and routing budget precheck; in Community its content stage is the core data-loss check without the Business deep inspector. Its declared assurance is a non-atomic, fail-open development precheck, not a qualified hard monetary cap.
unpromoted: A universal provider or model matrix: the Claude Messages protocol establishes one configured route, not a matrix, and this record does not assert that no other product generation path exists.
Centralized key custody: provider key fields are references.
Execution from the console as an accepted journey: the routing panel calls the execute API after explicit confirmation for models:routing:admin users. This source review did not execute that journey.
Budget authoring and deep content inspection on this path: both are Business capabilities, and Community only keeps enforcing stored budgets.
gaps: No executed provider or version row against a real counterpart exists.

claims.title: Managed-settings delivery
claims.boundedProposition: Render managed settings locally, validate and preview a policy document without writing any host, or serve one configured settings document from the gateway for authenticated pull. Fleet publishing, the signed artifact, attested check-in and drift are Business; Community answers those routes with 501 and names Business. Per-host application is external and never assumed.
conditions: The managed-settings connector declares a modeling-only boundary.
The CLI renders settings locally and labels that operation local.
Validate and dry-run write no host; without an observed-config source, dry-run says the effect was not diffed.
The Apps gateway serves one configured document to an authenticated bearer.
unpromoted: Fleet rollout and rollback.
Per-host application: nothing in Community proves that an endpoint applied the settings.
gaps: Defined tests describe local render, validate and dry-run, the Business refusal of fleet routes, and single-document gateway behavior, not host application; none was executed for this measurement. Until a real managed host adapter is covered by defined tests, copy must name render, preview and pull, never rollout.

claims.title: Read/write access inventory
claims.boundedProposition: Build a read and write access inventory over observed and permitted access edges, with per-edge attribution tiers, drift and attack-path queries, each read audited. Historical replay and authority acceptance are separate and unmeasured here.
conditions: The access-map module exposes graph, neighbor, drift and attack-path queries. Its access-evidence reads are internal and publish no route.
Observed and permitted (declared grant) flags are distinct inputs, and drift reports unexpected accesses and unused grants separately.
unpromoted: Historical reconstruction and authority acceptance.
Claim-level acceptance for the published roadmap sentence.
gaps: Module tests are source inventory; no executed export, stop or independent-reconstruction evidence exists.

claims.title: Claude Code session governance
claims.boundedProposition: When the operator configures the Claude Code hook enforcement point, it consults governed stop state before allowing, checks a firm caller identity and stored agent lifecycle decisions for each tenant that enables those checks, and routes reviewed tool use through the approval engine. A tenant can set its authored policy to observe mode for a bounded time; an unreadable stop state still denies in that mode. Break-glass is Business; Community answers its routes with 501.
conditions: The hook enforcement point reads governed kill-switch state before it allows an action, and an unreadable state denies.
Stop state, approvals and agent lifecycle decisions are governance-owned; the hook disposition policy is operator configuration.
Firm caller identity and agent lifecycle denial are per-tenant settings, off unless the tenant enables them.
unpromoted: A ratified composition with managed-settings-delivery: the overlap is plausible and is not asserted here.
Host-side policy constraints beyond the hook path.
Break-glass emergency access and agent identity federation.
gaps: This measurement does not execute the public hook-policy journey or establish host-wide constraints. No claim-level acceptance artifact is supplied.

claims.title: MCP catalog and governance
claims.boundedProposition: Admit and sign MCP server, connector and model entries through a governed catalog, with admission-boundary component test sources. Approval requires a verified admission only for a tenant whose admission policy requires signing; without that policy, admission is recorded in observe mode. Provisioning an approved entry onto infrastructure is Business. Interoperability with every external server is not asserted.
conditions: Catalog admission covers MCP, connector and model entries in the measured sources.
Signing is a catalog-owned surface when a catalog signing key is configured. Catalog activation forwards to deployment, which Community refuses and names Business.
The per-tenant admission policy is absent by default, which is observe mode: an entry can then be approved without a verified admission.
unpromoted: All-server interoperability and an executed version matrix against real counterparts.
gaps: This measurement supplies no executed external counterpart or version matrix and no claim-level acceptance artifact.

claims.title: FinOps controls that can act
claims.boundedProposition: Apply FinOps admission at composed production gates. In Community these gates enforce budgets stored before 1.0 while the FinOps module is on; Community can list and remove those budgets and refuses to create or change one. Reserve denies when the ledger cannot establish admission; enforcing exhausted budgets deny. The configured inference proxy reserves an estimate before forwarding, then commits observed cost or releases the hold. Legacy CheckBudget keeps its fail-open read-error behavior, and no composed gate calls it.
conditions: The in-process voice, evals, model-route, durable MCP task and session-launch gates call Reserve with the deny-on-unreachable posture. Their zero estimate evaluates admission without creating a monetary hold; an unbound evals gate allows until composition binds FinOps. Orchestration is a Business capability, and Community composes no orchestration budget gate.

The inference proxy is off on a new install. Once it is on, its budget gate is on by default and reserves a real estimate before forwarding. Finalization commits measured spend or releases the hold; settlement errors after the effect are logged and the hold expires, rather than undoing the completed effect.

Legacy CheckBudget may return allow with a read error. Session-launch availability is configured separately: unset or invalid is fail-closed, only an explicit fail-open setting lets a launch proceed when the ledger is unreachable, and a definitive cap always denies. Reserve itself still uses the deny posture. The development Chat route declares a non-atomic, fail-open precheck assurance, not a qualified hard cap.
Gate decisions carry provider-neutral references and money-free refusal reasons. Internal reservations and inference settlement carry the estimate and actual cost.
In Community, creating or updating a budget or a spend limit is refused with a Business edition answer; listing, reading and deleting a stored budget stay available.
unpromoted: A universal hard-cap guarantee across every actuation path, including configured session availability and development Chat execution.
Claim-level acceptance of the reservation, dispatch and settlement journey: source composition and test inventory alone do not establish it.
Budget authoring and team and project spend analysis: Business capabilities, not reviewed here.
gaps: The composed Reserve and inference commit/release paths and the Community authoring refusal exist at the measured source. This source review supplies no executed claim-level reservation/settlement acceptance artifact.

claims.title: Compliance evidence mapping
claims.boundedProposition: Read and export, as JSON or CSV, the compliance evidence packages already stored; each package read and export is audited. Framework mapping, assessment, sealing and OSCAL export are Business and answer 501 in Community. Mapping to a framework is not certification against it.
conditions: Stored evidence reads and exports are owned by the compliance module in the measured sources. Mapping to a framework is not certification.
Community holds no framework catalog and refuses framework views, sealing and OSCAL export, naming Business.
unpromoted: Certification or conformance against any named framework.
Historical reconstruction with integrity, provenance, completeness and semantic replay separated.
gaps: No executed reconstruction evidence exists and no certification is claimed.

claims.title: Kill-switch deny gate with dual control
claims.boundedProposition: Stop agent activity through governed stop gates. On each surface the operator configures, the hook enforcement point, the inference proxy, the MCP gateway forward and the session launch gate refuse when stop state cannot be read. Lifting a stop takes a fresh approval by two distinct people, which an approval policy cannot lower. The circuit breaker is a Business runtime-security capability: Community links no breaker, so its gate never denies, and a Community server refuses to start with the breaker switched on.
conditions: The enforcement points fail closed on a stop-state read error; event delivery instead parks non-governance deliveries so approvals and findings still flow.

Re-enable is a two-step request: the first call opens a critical approval, and the stop lifts only once at least two distinct human approvers are re-counted in the same transaction; an unreviewed prior incident of the same scope blocks a further re-enable, and there is no break-glass path around it.
An operator command surface reports and lists stop state; it is read-only, and engage, re-enable and review are separate governed API calls.
unpromoted: Claim-level acceptance of the stop and two-person re-enable journey: tests present in source are not an execution receipt.
Circuit-breaker behavior with a Business engine, including its read-error posture, is not reviewed here.
Host-wide enforcement: a surface that is not configured consults no stop state.
gaps: The stop and re-enable tests are source anchors; no claim-level execution receipt exists.

claims.title: Self-hosted control plane
claims.boundedProposition: Run the Community control plane on infrastructure the operator owns. Kubernetes fleet management requires Business. The supported deployment and recovery matrix is not qualified by code inventory.
conditions: A self-hosted boot and licensing path exists in the command tree, and the license is persisted and displayed without gating Community features. The Community source holds no Kubernetes operator or Helm chart; they are distributed with Business.
unpromoted: Install, interrupt, swap, migration, startup and credential recovery with data and authority intact.
Any qualified deployment or recovery matrix.
gaps: Code inventory does not qualify the deployment or recovery matrix, and no such run was executed at any inspected object.
